title: Agents vs automations
slides: Pick the wrong one and you pay for brains you don't need, or rules that keep breaking.
If this happens, do that. Same steps every time. Cheap and reliable.
It reads the situation, chooses the next step, and handles messy input like a free-text message.
The task never changes: copying data, sending alerts, filing documents.
The input varies: answering customer questions, sorting enquiries, drafting replies.
Use it next time someone pitches you AI.
caption:
Not everything needs an AI agent. I've built both, and a simple Zapier automation beats an agent most of the time.

An automation follows rules: a new Gmail order becomes a Google Sheets row, the same way every time. An AI agent makes decisions: it reads a messy WhatsApp message at 11pm and works out what the customer wants.

My rule: if the steps never change, automate it. If it needs judgement, use an agent. Not sure? Start with the automation.

Save this for the next time someone pitches you AI.
